prompt: This pizza base came out (thin) than the one we baked on Sunday.
explanation_ru: В односложном прилагательном «thin» конечная согласная «n» удваивается перед суффиксом -er: thinner.

prompt: Is the station café usually (busy) on Saturday mornings than on weekdays?
explanation_ru: У двусложного прилагательного «busy» конечная «y» после согласной меняется на «i» перед -er: busier.

prompt: My cousin drives (carefully) than before after scratching his bumper on a post.
explanation_ru: Наречия с суффиксом -ly образуют сравнительную степень с помощью «more»: more carefully.

prompt: This roof leak isn't small; it is (bad) than the crack in autumn.
explanation_ru: Прилагательное «bad» образует сравнительную степень не по правилу: worse.

prompt: Booking rail tickets on this phone app is ___ than using the old website.
explanation_ru: У «easy» конечная «y» меняется на «i» и добавляется -er (easier); типичные ошибки — «more easy» и написание «easyer».

prompt: We took a more big tent so all four friends could sleep inside.
answer: We took a bigger tent so all four friends could sleep inside.
accepted_answers: We took a bigger tent so all four friends could sleep inside.
explanation_ru: Типичная ошибка — «more big»: односложное прилагательное «big» требует суффикса -er с удвоением согласной (bigger).

prompt: That yellow rain jacket costs (little) than the branded one and folds (neatly) into my rucksack than my old coat.
explanation_ru: У «little» неправильная сравнительная степень «less», а наречие «neatly» на -ly образует сравнение с «more» (more neatly).

prompt: Did anyone else feel the main character grew (unhappy) after the wedding than he was in the opening chapter?
explanation_ru: Прилагательное «unhappy» обычно образует форму через замену «y» на «i» перед -er (unhappier), хотя вариант «more unhappy» также допустим.

prompt: Walking beside the hedge took (long) than usual, yet we didn't mind because the frozen footpath felt (slippery) than the main road.
explanation_ru: Краткое наречие «long» принимает -er (longer), а трёхсложное «slippery» чаще используется с «more» (more slippery), хотя форма «slipperier» тоже встречается.

prompt: Standing outside the locked holiday cottage in the rain, our spare key proved ___ than the tourist map.
explanation_ru: Прилагательные с суффиксом -ful (useful) всегда образуют сравнительную степень через «more» (more useful), а не через -er.

prompt: Most students didn't enjoy the long talk because the hands-on workshop explained the steps ___ than the slides.
explanation_ru: После глагола «explained» нужно наречие «clearly» в сравнительной степени — more clearly; формы «clearlier» не существует, а «more clear» — прилагательное.

prompt: My elder sister speaks Spanish far better than I do, even though we attended the same school.
answer: My elder sister speaks Spanish far better than I do, even though we attended the same school.
accepted_answers: My elder sister speaks Spanish far better than I do, even though we attended the same school.
explanation_ru: Ошибки нет: «elder» правильно стоит перед существительным-родственником (my elder sister), а «better» — верная сравнительная степень от наречия «well».

prompt: Kofi got a pay rise at the garage while his rent and bills stayed the same. His sister says he no longer worries about the end of the month.
options: Kofi is better off than before, and he handles his monthly bills more easily.
Kofi is gooder off than before, and he handles his monthly bills more easy.
Kofi is worse off than before, and he handles his monthly bills less easily.
Kofi is the best off than before, and he handles his monthly bills most easily.
explanation_ru: Верный первый вариант: «good» имеет неправильную форму «better» (better off), а наречие «easily» образует сравнение с «more» (more easily).

prompt: Thanks to extra funding, the first repair schedule isn't as realistic as our revised timetable. → Thanks to extra funding, our revised timetable is …
answer: Thanks to extra funding, our revised timetable is more realistic than the first repair schedule.
accepted_answers: Thanks to extra funding, our revised timetable is more realistic than the first repair schedule.
explanation_ru: Многосложное прилагательное «realistic» образует сравнительную степень с «more» и союзом «than»: more realistic than.

prompt: During the club vote, Mei took (cautious) view of everyone on the board. She hadn't seen the final accounts yet, so she asked questions (carefully) than the treasurer did. When the numbers arrived, however, her advice worked (well) than the chair's rough guess. Everyone agreed to follow her plan.
explanation_ru: Прилагательные на -ous («cautious») требуют «the most», наречие «carefully» — «more», а наречие «well» имеет неправильную сравнительную степень better.

prompt: "Did Dawid speak (fluently) than Leena in the debate final?" "He spoke smoothly, yet he answered the judges' questions (badly) than she did. He offered (few) real examples than her, so his closing argument didn't convince anyone. Honestly, I expect Leena to win."
explanation_ru: Наречие «fluently» образует форму с «more», у «badly» неправильная форма «worse», а с исчисляемым существительным «examples» употребляется fewer.

prompt: Our youth sports grant has been updated for the new season. Among all local schemes, this version is (fair) for small village clubs. The application rules are (clear) than before, and teams spend (little) time filling in forms. You don't need an accountant to apply.
explanation_ru: Короткие «fair» и «clear» принимают -est и -er (the fairest, clearer), а перед неисчисляемым «time» стоит неправильная сравнительная форма less.

prompt: Residents praised the second transport report for listening to both cyclists and drivers. Its tone feels (balanced) than the angry newsletter from spring, and the new bus route reaches (far) along the valley. However, the committee didn't set a single date, so the repairs will probably progress (slowly) than we hoped. Without clear deadlines, commuters will quickly lose patience.
explanation_ru: Прилагательные-причастия на -ed («balanced») образуют сравнение с «more», для расстояния у «far» возможны further и farther, а наречие «slowly» требует «more».
